home.headline: PAUSE.
home.actionLine: PAUSE before you Pay, Sign, Share or Travel.
home.secondaryCta: Practice with a foreign employment offer
home.heroDescription: When a foreign-employment opportunity asks you to act, PAUSE: identify the provider, authenticate independently, understand the incentive, stop the rush, and verify the evidence before acting.

pause.title: The PAUSE Framework
pause.subtitle: Five steps to evaluate a foreign employment offer

provider.label: Provider
provider.question: Who is providing this information?
provider.emphasis: Identify the recruiter, agency, sender and claimed provider.
provider.description: The first step is to understand where the information came from. The person who sent the message may not be the original source. A Facebook post, WhatsApp message or recruitment agent is not the final authority.
provider.tip: The sender and the original source can be different.

authenticate.label: Authenticate
authenticate.question: Can this be confirmed from an official or independent source?
authenticate.emphasis: Move to a source not controlled by the original sender.
authenticate.description: Don't ask for confirmation from the same person or organization. Check with official government websites, departments or independent sources.
authenticate.tip: Asking the same source for confirmation is not confirmation.

incentive.label: Understand the Incentive
incentive.question: Who benefits if I believe this or take action?
incentive.emphasis: Recognize incentives without labelling every incentive as fraud.
incentive.description: Someone benefiting doesn't automatically mean it's fraud. But understanding who benefits helps you stay more careful.
incentive.tip: Benefit ≠ fraud, but understanding benefit = safety.

rush.label: Stop the Rush
rush.question: Why am I being rushed?
rush.emphasis: Treat urgency as a reason to slow down.
rush.description: "Pay today or lose the job" — this is pressure. Real opportunities give time to verify. Rushing is a strategy to make you act without checking.
rush.tip: Rush = reason to check, not reason to hurry.

evidence.label: Evidence
evidence.question: What evidence can I check before acting?
evidence.description: Check concrete details such as employer, agency, post, salary, location, fees and approval information. A matching logo or company name alone is not enough.
evidence.tip: One matching detail doesn't create trust — compare multiple fields.

practice.title: Practice Scenarios
practice.subtitle: Learn to use PAUSE in realistic foreign employment situations

scenario.proceedWarning: Stop! Acting in a rush increases risk. Protect yourself by completing each step of PAUSE.
scenario.verifyInstruction: Now verify this information from an official source

verified.title: Officially Verified
verified.description: The information matches official sources. But always stay alert and re-check when new information comes.
verified.action: You may proceed, but re-check all details before signing any contract.

mismatch.title: Information Mismatch
mismatch.description: There are differences between the claimed information and official sources. This is a serious warning sign.
mismatch.action: Do not pay and do not sign documents. Seek more information or contact the Department of Foreign Employment.

cannotVerify.title: Could Not Verify
cannotVerify.description: The available evidence is not sufficient to confirm or deny the information. Uncertainty does not mean you must decide now.
cannotVerify.action: Don't rush. Seek more information, ask the department, or consult a trusted person.

verify.title: Official Verification Routes
verify.subtitle: Use these official sources to verify foreign employment information
verify.importantNoteText: A matching logo or company name alone is not enough. Compare multiple fields so that one copied detail cannot create false confidence.
verify.disclaimer: This application does not replace official government systems. It teaches you where and how to verify.

about.title: About PAUSE
about.whatIsText: PAUSE is an interactive information literacy tool that teaches people seeking foreign employment in Nepal how to independently verify offers.
notWhatItems: Not a replacement for the Department of Foreign Employment or any official government database.
Not a guarantee that a job opportunity is genuine.
Not a service that asks for passport or citizenship documents for normal learning activities.
about.methodologyText: The PAUSE framework teaches five repeatable questions: P — Provider, A — Authenticate, U — Understand the Incentive, S — Stop the Rush, and E — Evidence. The most important learning outcome is not memorizing the acronym; it is demonstrating a change in verification behaviour before paying money, signing documents, sharing sensitive information, or travelling.
principlesList: Never make urgency proof of fraud; make it a reason to pause.
Never turn inability to verify into certainty about falsity.
Always teach the next verification action.
about.builtFor: Built for foreign-employment information literacy in Nepal

footer.disclaimer: This application does not replace official government systems.

highSalary.title: High Salary Job Offer
highSalary.description: A high-salary offer for a Construction Supervisor position in Dubai received via Facebook. Is it genuine?
highSalary.messagePreview: Construction Supervisor job open in Dubai! Salary Rs. 1,50,000 per month, free food and accommodation. Pay Rs. 2,00,000 by tomorrow or we give it to another candidate. Contact: Bright Future Manpower

p.opt1: This offer is reliable because it has many likes and shares on Facebook.
p.opt2: The sender and the claimed company/agency might be different — I need to figure out who the original sender is first.
p.opt3: I already know this agency, so it's reliable.
p.explanation: Having likes and shares on Facebook doesn't mean the information is true. The first step is to separate who sent the message from whether the claimed company is genuine.
p.feedbackCorrect: Good! You understood the difference between the sender and the original source. A Facebook post is not an official confirmation.
p.feedbackIncorrect: Being popular on Facebook doesn't mean the information is true. The sender and the claimed company can be different.

a.opt1: I'll ask on the same Facebook page — they will confirm it.
a.opt2: I'll go to the agency's office to ask.
a.opt3: I'll check the agency's name and license number from the Department of Foreign Employment's website.
a.explanation: Asking the same source for confirmation is not confirmation. You must verify from an independent, official source like the Department of Foreign Employment (DOFE) website.
a.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! The DOFE website is an independent, official source where you can check the agency's license and status.
a.feedbackIncorrect: Asking the same source doesn't provide independent verification. Verify from an official government source.

u.opt1: The agency is asking for a fee of Rs. 2,00,000 — they benefit if I pay, but this doesn't automatically mean it's a scam. However, understanding this makes me more careful.
u.opt2: Nobody benefits — this is a service.
u.opt3: Since they benefit, this is definitely a scam.
u.explanation: Someone benefiting doesn't automatically mean it's a scam. Legitimate agencies also charge fees. But understanding who benefits and why helps you stay more careful.
u.feedbackCorrect: Correct! Understanding benefit doesn't mean doubting everyone — it means staying careful.
u.feedbackIncorrect: Benefiting and scamming are not the same thing. Even legitimate businesses have fees, but it's important to understand them.

s.opt1: I have to pay by tomorrow — I'll hurry otherwise I'll lose the job.
s.opt2: The deadline of tomorrow is pressure — it's a reason to verify, not a reason to hurry.
s.opt3: If there's a deadline, it must be real — fake offers don't have deadlines.
s.explanation: "Pay tomorrow or it goes to someone else" is a pressure tactic. Real opportunities give time to verify. Treat the rush as a reason to check.
s.feedbackCorrect: Correct! The rush is a reason to verify. Real employers give time to check.
s.feedbackIncorrect: Having a deadline doesn't mean the offer is real. Pressure is a tactic to make you act without checking.

e.opt1: The document provided by the agency is enough evidence.
e.opt2: The Facebook post has the company's logo, so it's real.
e.opt3: I'll compare details like employer, agency, post, salary, fees, and approval info from the DOFE website.
e.explanation: A matching logo or company name alone is not enough. You must compare all fields — employer, agency license, post, salary, fees — against the official source.
e.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Comparing multiple fields means one copied detail cannot create false confidence.
e.feedbackIncorrect: Logos and documents are easy to copy. Compare multiple fields from an official source.

genuine.title: Genuine EPS Job Opportunity
genuine.description: An offer for a factory worker position in South Korea under the EPS program from a recruitment agency office. PAUSE can confirm real opportunities too.
genuine.messagePreview: Applications are open for factory worker positions at Samsung C&T Corporation in South Korea under the EPS program. Salary Rs. 80,000–1,00,000 per month. Fees as per government rates. EPS application deadline is approaching.

p.opt1: This info is from a licensed recruitment agency office — I'll verify the agency's license first.
p.opt2: Because it's in an office, it's definitely real.
p.opt3: The EPS program is a government program, so there's no need to verify.
p.explanation: Being in an office or using a government program's name doesn't automatically make it reliable. The first step is to identify the provider and check their license.
p.feedbackCorrect: Good! Even in an agency office, checking the license is a good practice.
p.feedbackIncorrect: Having an office or using a government program name doesn't guarantee the information is true. Always verify.

a.opt1: I'll ask at the agency office — they'll confirm it themselves.
a.opt2: I'll verify the agency's license, EPS program details, and Samsung C&T's listing from the DOFE website.
a.opt3: I'll ask friends — they have gone before.
a.explanation: The DOFE website and EPS program info are independent, official sources. The agency office or friends are not independent sources.
a.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! DOFE and EPS program info are official independent sources.
a.feedbackIncorrect: The agency office or friends are not independent sources. Verify from an official government source.

u.opt1: If the agency charges a fee, it's a scam.
u.opt2: The agency charges fees as per government rates — this is a legitimate business practice, but I'll compare the fee amount with government rates.
u.explanation: Legitimate agencies also charge fees — it's a business practice. The important thing is to compare whether the fee matches government rates.
u.feedbackCorrect: Correct! It's wise to compare the fee with government rates.
u.feedbackIncorrect: Charging a fee and scamming are not the same. Compare with government rates.

s.opt1: The EPS application deadline is near — this is a real deadline, but I'll still take time to verify.
s.opt2: If the deadline is near, I'll pay immediately.
s.opt3: Because there's a deadline, it's fake.
s.explanation: The EPS program has a real application deadline — it's not a pressure tactic. But even with a real deadline, it's always good to take time to verify.
s.feedbackCorrect: Good! Even with a real deadline, taking time to verify is smart.
s.feedbackIncorrect: The EPS program might have a real date, but that doesn't mean you should act without checking.

e.opt1: I'll compare agency license, EPS program listing, Samsung C&T listing, salary range, and fee rates from DOFE — all official sources.
e.opt2: The letter provided by the agency is enough.
e.opt3: Samsung is a big company, so there's no need to verify.
e.explanation: Just a big company's name or an agency's letter is not enough. All details — license, program listing, salary, fees — must be compared from an official source.
e.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! You showed the habit of comparing all important fields from an official source.
e.feedbackIncorrect: A big company name or document alone is not enough. Verify multiple fields from an official source.
